text:
maria: Heads up — since ~02:15 UTC we've seen intermittent packet loss on the overlay between gpu-pool-* nodes in us-west-2. Training jobs showing stalls and retransmits. ping between nodes shows ~3-7% loss intermittently. Affects pods with large MTU traffic (batched token streams).
net-bot: ALERT: encap_drop_rate spike on cluster-us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T02:16Z (>0.7%). See /alerts/encap-181543.
simon: Which nodes exactly? single AZ or cross-AZ? is this on Cilium/eBPF datapath or kube-proxy?
maria: Mostly az-b & az-c. Node examples: gpu-usw2-azb-12, gpu-usw2-azb-17, gpu-usw2-azc-03. Kernel 5.10.147, cilium 1.14.0, docker runtime. Geneve encap used (we opted for geneve for MTU flexibility).
kai: Can you run iperf3 between two affected pods (hostNetwork=false) and a quick tcpdump on the host for geneve frames? Also check ethtool -k on the NICs (GSO/GRO settings).
maria: Running now. iperf3 shows bandwidth swinging and retransmits:
```
$ iperf3 -c 10.2.0.8 -t 30
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth       Retr  Cwnd
[  5]   0.00-1.00   sec   110 MBytes   921 Mbits/sec    12   58.7 KBytes
[  5]   1.00-2.00   sec    96 MBytes   805 Mbits/sec     3   59.2 KBytes
... spikes in retransmits every ~10s
```
jess: tcpdump from host (partial):
```
13:22:11.123456 IP 10.2.0.5 > 10.2.0.8: UDP, length 64
13:22:11.123457 geneve: vni 0x0 - frag? - outer src 172.31.46.12 > 172.31.50.9: UDP, length 128
13:22:21.223334 IP 10.2.0.5 > 10.2.0.8: UDP, length 1500
13:22:21.223335 geneve: outer len mismatch, drop
```
simon: "outer len mismatch" and short frames look like GSO/GRO interactions with encapsulation; GSO may create large skbs that get chopped by encap and the NIC offloads. Any recent kernel or mellanox firmware updates rolled in?
kai: We actually rolled a Mellanox driver update on az-b last night (firmware 5.32 -> 5.34) to address small SR-IOV regressions. I've seen similar with VXLAN/GSO combos where offload leads to encap packet truncation. Quick check: on host run `ethtool -k eth0` and `cat /sys/module/udp_tunnel/parameters/gro_max_size` (if present).
maria: ethtool -k shows gso: on, gro: on. Also found this in dmesg on one node: `mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0 net mlx5_0: Unexpected GSO size after encapsulation, dropping skb`
jess: That log pretty much nails it. Short-term mitigation: disable GSO/GRO on host NICs for affected nodes or disable offload on the tunnel device. Example: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off` — will increase CPU but should stop those drops.
simon: Can we instead tweak Cilium tunnel fragmentation or set lower tunnel_mtu to avoid GSO creation? Might be safer than turning off offloads cluster-wide.
kai: Agreed. Two options: 1) reduce cilium/geneve tunnel MTU (e.g., from 1450 -> 1400) and cordon/drain a node to test; 2) toggle offload on 1-2 nodes as a canary.
oncall: I'm taking ownership for the canary. I'll cordon gpu-usw2-azb-17, drain, toggle offloads, bring back up during a short window. Scheduling now (5m). Ticket INC-2026-112 created.
net-bot: NOTE: mitigation applied to gpu-usw2-azb-17 at 02:26Z — ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off. Monitoring.
maria: After disabling GSO on that host, iperf3 stabilized (no retransmits in 2x 30s runs) and training pod bandwidth steady. Observed CPU bump on host but acceptable for now.
net-bot: encap_drop_rate reduced to 0.05% cluster-us-west-2 at 02:38Z.
jess: Plan of action: 1) run host offload toggle canary on 2 more nodes in az-b, 2) evaluate kernel/driver rollback or vendor fix for mlx5 encapsulation GSO handling, 3) add Cilium conservative tunnel_mtu fallback and monitoring rule to alert earlier.
maria: Thanks — I'll capture logs and prepare a short postmortem. Will also loop in infra-team and Mellanox vendor if driver fix needed. :thumbsup:
